study_material.title: Pipes and Cisterns - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: Pipes and cisterns is time-and-work with a twist: inlet pipes do positive work (filling) and outlet/leak pipes do negative work (emptying). Add the signed rates and invert to get the filling time.
learning_objectives: Combine inlet and outlet rates with correct signs
Find leak rates from slowed filling times
Handle pipes opened or closed at different times

concepts.heading: 1. Signed Rates
concepts.body: An inlet filling in x hours contributes +1/x per hour; an outlet emptying in y hours contributes -1/y. Net rate = sum. If the net is positive the tank fills in 1/net hours; if negative, it empties.

concepts.heading: 2. Leak Problems
concepts.body: If a pipe alone fills in x hours but takes x' hours with a leak, the leak's rate = 1/x - 1/x'. The leak alone empties a full tank in the reciprocal of that. Example: fill 8 h alone, 10 h with leak: leak rate = 1/8 - 1/10 = 1/40, leak empties in 40 h.

concepts.heading: 3. Staggered Opening
concepts.body: When pipes open or close at different times, split the timeline into phases. Compute the work (tank fraction) in each phase, track the cumulative total, and solve the final phase for the unknown time.

concepts.heading: 4. Partial Tanks
concepts.body: A tank already 2/5 full that must be emptied or filled needs only that fraction of work. Time = fraction / net rate. Sign of the net rate tells you whether it fills or drains.

formulas: Net rate = sum of 1/fill times - sum of 1/empty times
Time for fraction f of tank = f / net rate
shortcut_methods: Use LCM of the given times as tank capacity in units
Keep emptying rates negative from the start - never juggle signs later
Phase problems: litres (units) filled so far is the only state you need
common_mistakes: Adding an outlet's rate with a positive sign
Ignoring the already-filled fraction in partial-tank problems
study_material.summary: Treat filling as positive work and emptying as negative, sum rates, and divide the remaining fraction by the net rate.
quick_revision_notes: LCM units make phase problems clean

questions.question: Two inlets fill a 216-litre tank in 12 and 18 minutes. With a waste pipe also open, the tank fills in 216/21 minutes. How many litres per minute does the waste pipe remove?
questions.explanation: Inlet rates: 216/12 = 18 and 216/18 = 12 L/min, total 30. Net rate = 216 divided by 216/21 = 21 L/min, so the waste pipe removes 30 - 21 = 9 L/min.
